messages:
sam.presales: Quick sync — AcmeRetail POC hit a handshake blocker. Node SDK streaming: after the initial SSE connect we get INVALID_HANDSHAKE_SIGNATURE and stream closes. Anyone seen this with signed payloads + SSO token exchange?

elena.solutions: hm, I saw something similar with an edge proxy that strips headers. Can you paste the minimal client-side handshake and the server log snippet?

sam.presales: here's the client side (simplified):
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` ,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Redwood-Signature': signature
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-13b', streaming: true })
});
```
And server error from customer proxy: `handshake: verify signature failed: INVALID_HANDSHAKE_SIGNATURE`

raj.eng-runtime: two common causes: 1) signature header is being removed/normalized by a proxy (common with some corporate gateways), 2) timestamp/window mismatch when using signed payloads. Also check that you sign the canonical payload we expect — small differences (whitespace/newlines) can break it.

elena.solutions: also verify the signing key version. We rotate keys and accept v1/v2 signatures if configured; older clients might still be using v0.

sam.presales: Acme's infra team says headers are preserved. We tried signing the raw JSON and the same body with pretty spacing, both fail. Timestamp is within 10s.

raj.eng-runtime: can you dump the exact canonical string you're signing? It should be: `timestamp + '.' + base64url(payload)` and then HMAC with the edge signing key. If you do HMAC on the pretty-printed JSON you'll get a mismatch.

sam.presales: dumping now, sample canonical string: `1612345678.eyJtb2RlbCI6ImhlbGxvIn0` — looks right?

raj.eng-runtime: that looks plausible. Two extra checks: 1) make sure the token exchange step (SSO -> short-lived streaming creds) returns the same client timestamp tolerance as the signing service; 2) if the customer routes through an API gateway, some gateways will change Content-Type or re-encode the body for logging which affects signature. For debugging: try calling our handshake endpoint directly from a laptop (no proxy) to isolate.

lisa.sales: on the sales side — if we recommend short-lived streaming creds instead of signed payloads, any product restrictions or pricing impacts? Acme asked if enabling signed payloads costs extra.

raj.eng-runtime: no pricing delta tied to signed payloads. The only unit cost is tokens during streaming plus connection overhead. Signed handshake adds a tiny CPU/HMAC check and maybe ~15–40ms of latency on the handshake path. For Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs we sometimes recommend pre-warmed connections or ephemeral creds to avoid repeated handshakes.

elena.solutions: workaround for POC: enable ephemeral creds (STS-like flow) for the streaming session, skip header signing for now, and use signed callbacks for webhook delivery instead. That keeps security posture without the client-side canonical signing complexity.

devops-bot: vault: added secret `acme/edge-signing-key-v2` to team/redwood-presales (rotate manually after POC) :white_check_mark:

sam.presales: good call. If we do ephemeral creds, what's the minimum TTL we should recommend for demo? 60s? 5min?

raj.eng-runtime: for demos 5m is fine (less churn). For production, 30s–2m is typical depending on threat model. Also include an auto-refresh logic in the SDK sample so reconnects are smooth.

elena.solutions: I'll draft a one-pager runbook: reproduce steps, workaround, sample curl/js snippets, and a checklist for customer infra (proxy passthrough, header allowlist, canonical signing example). Raj, can you add the canonical signing snippet to the runbook?

raj.eng-runtime: will do — I'll paste the canonicalization + verify snippet in Node and Go.

lisa.sales: I'll schedule a joint call with Acme infra + our eng tomorrow 10am PT. Sam, can you share their contact and a short agenda?

sam.presales: sharing contact in DM. Agenda: quick repro, decide ephemeral creds vs signed payloads for POC, follow-up runbook + handoff. Thanks all :pray:

elena.solutions: +1 — sounds good.

sam.presales: thanks — I'll update the thread with the runbook link once ready.
